Register the ""disable virtualization in an emergency"" callback just
before KVM enables virtualization in hardware
need to keep the callbacks registered while KVM happens to be loaded
is inactive
column2: i.e. if KVM hasn't enabled virtualization.

column1: Note
column2: unregistering the callback every time the last VM is destroyed could

column1: have measurable latency due to the synchronize_rcu() needed to ensure all
references to the callback are dropped before KVM is unloaded.  But the
latency should be a small fraction of the total latency of disabling
virtualization across all CPUs
to completely eliminate the runtime overhead.
Add a pointer in kvm_x86_ops to allow vendor code to provide its callback.
There is no reason to force vendor code to do the registration
way KVM would need a new kvm_x86_ops hook.
